title: Risks and complications
body:
## General risks

[Placeholder] All medical and cosmetic procedures carry some degree of risk, regardless of how routine they may be considered. This page outlines the general risks and possible complications associated with treatments offered at Dr Tranter Aesthetics, in addition to the treatment-specific risks discussed during consultation.

[Placeholder] General risks associated with non-surgical and device-led treatments may include bruising, swelling, redness, tenderness, temporary discolouration, and in rare cases, infection, scarring, asymmetry or an allergic reaction to a product used during treatment.

## Injectable treatments

[Placeholder] Injectable treatments carry additional specific risks, including but not limited to vascular occlusion, lumps or nodules under the skin, migration of product, and rare but serious complications affecting vision or tissue health. These risks are discussed individually and in full at consultation, before any treatment is booked.

[Placeholder] Patients are screened for contraindications, including pregnancy, breastfeeding, active skin infection, and certain autoimmune or bleeding conditions, prior to any injectable treatment being considered.

## Device-led and laser treatments

[Placeholder] Radiofrequency, laser and light-based treatments carry risks including burns, pigment changes (both lightening and darkening of the skin), prolonged redness, and in rare cases, scarring. Suitability is assessed based on skin type, tone and medical history.

[Placeholder] Downtime and recovery vary significantly between device-led treatments; expected downtime and warning signs to monitor for are provided in writing following every procedure.

## Individual results and no guarantee

[Placeholder] Results vary between individuals and cannot be guaranteed. Photographs, descriptions and expected outcomes discussed at consultation are general guides only and do not represent a guaranteed result for any specific patient.

[Placeholder] Patients are encouraged to ask questions at any stage of the consultation or treatment process, and are never obligated to proceed with a recommended treatment.

## What to do if you have concerns after treatment

[Placeholder] Patients who experience unexpected pain, worsening symptoms, or any concern following a procedure should contact the clinic immediately using the emergency contact details provided at the time of treatment. Do not wait for a scheduled follow-up appointment if you have an urgent concern.
